cards.subject: The Dragonmaw Garrison
lines: This was the top of Blackrock Spire and it was orc ground. The first room of the raid still carries the name, and is still full of orcs.

After Deathwing left for Draenor his children were sent to take the Blackrock orcs as their own army. The fortress at the summit stopped being a garrison and became a laboratory, and its soldiers became egg-guards.

cards.subject: There is no portal on the mountain
lines: You get in by touching a rock at the end of a hall beside the Blackrock Spire entrance, and it puts you on the peak, past the whole upper dungeon.
In vanilla it only answered to somebody Drakkisath had branded.
The door is a shortcut, not an entrance.

cards.subject: The first room is a demolition job
lines: The thirty black dragon eggs cannot be hurt by players. Only by him.
So you take an orb off his handler, mind-control the boss, and pilot him into smashing his master's clutch while the rest of the raid holds off the room.
Then he breaks free and turns on you.

cards.subject: He apologises before he kills you
lines: You have to talk to him to start it. "I... I have failed. The Lord of Bla... The Lord of Blackrock is too powerful."
He asks you to kill him, and then buffs the entire raid with effectively unlimited mana so that you can do it fast enough.
He is fuelling his own execution.

cards.subject: A gift you cannot refuse
lines: Every fifteen seconds he hands somebody double damage and instant casts. Then they die and explode.
Healers get it too.
The correct play is to sprint away from everyone you were keeping alive, before the timer runs out.

cards.subject: The one true rogue moment
lines: Two rooms on the way to Broodlord are wired with devices that cut movement, attack and cast speed to a fifth, while whelps respawn without end.
Rogues stealth ahead and disarm them while forty people wait.
"None of your kind should be here. You've doomed only yourselves!"

cards.subject: There is a working alchemy lab in here
lines: One of only two in the old world, added three months after the raid opened so guilds could brew on site.
It is the honest signal of what this wing is.
Not a lair. A workshop, with technicians and spellbinders standing along the walls.

cards.subject: A different monster each lockout
lines: He has five breath weapons, one per dragonflight, and uses two of them. The pair is fixed for the life of that instance and rerolled on the next.
The boss your guild learned last week is not the boss standing there this week.

cards.subject: Collect all five and you stop being a player
lines: He stacks five coloured afflictions across the raid — disease, poison, magic, curse, and one that just stuns you.
Hold all five at once and you turn into a hostile elite drakonid. It cannot be dispelled.
Your own raid has to kill you.

cards.subject: The man on the throne is the dragon
lines: The last chamber has a human nobleman sitting at the far end of it, and you have to walk up and speak to him to begin.
He is Nefarian, eldest son of Deathwing.
He has already spoken to you twice on the way in without ever showing you a scale.

cards.subject: The fight reads your raid roster
lines: Paladins are forced to cast a protective blessing on Nefarian himself. Warlocks summon infernals against their own raid.
Priests' heals turn into damage on whoever they heal, and hunters' weapons are drained to nothing mid-fight.
It only calls the classes actually present.

cards.subject: The floor gets back up
lines: The first phase is forty-two drakonids, one of every colour he has bred.
At twenty percent he raises all of them again.
The ground you spent ten minutes clearing stands up underneath you.

cards.subject: Look out, and then look down
lines: The final chamber opens onto Searing Gorge from near the peak — one of the widest views in the old world, with an invisible wall holding you in.
Then look at the throne itself. It is a smashed copy of the one in the Imperial Seat far below.
He took the dwarf king's furniture and broke it to fit.
